newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares close at new record high.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares close at new record high.

text.p: Estonian shares climbed to record highs for the second straight day on Friday as the bullish market responded positively to the half-year results from key banking stocks.
The Talse index gained 1.28 percent on Friday to close at a record high of 282.60 and overall market volume was 52.4 million kroons.
Hansapank, was the active stock in trade of 14 million kroons as it gained 3.3 kroons to 152.70.
It released its half-year results on Thursday after the bourse closed. It has also said it will raise its 1997 profit forecast.
Hoiupank, which posted a record June profit yesterday, continued rising and closed two kroons higher at 156 kroons in trade worth 11.7 million kroons.
But Tallinna Pank suffered, falling 1.10 kroons to 63.10 kroons.
Dealers said its June financial results, which showed a profit of 4.4 million kroons, were not so impressive and that speculative interest over a possible merger with Hoiupank had vanished.
Local media reported earlier that Hoiupank and Tallinna Pank had started merger talks, but Tallinna yesterday announced it was not considering a merger in Estonia.
Tallinna also slipped in the wake of an announcement that it wants to take over Latvia's Saules Banka. The market has been cautious because details are not yet known, dealers said.
Uhispank also released its half-year results and said it will raise its 1997 profit forecast in August. The bank saw moderate trade to gain 0.04 kroons to 53.69 kroons.
Forekspank gained 2.4 kroons to 197.15 in trade of seven million kroons although its results are not out yet.
The free market turned over 7.5 million kroons and Tallinna Kaubamaja was the most active in trade of 3.3 million kroons.
